description:
Found by the Callables session while building fz-sc8.144 (develop 32a14dda4, interp and run).

Probe:
  defmodule H do
    defmacro m() do
      try do 7 rescue error -> raise(error) end
    end
  end
  defmodule Main do
    import H
    def main(), do: IO.inspect(m())
  end
  Main.main()

Elixir prints 7. fz reports six internal/unresolved-wait errors at <generated> (a call's return type, function definition, expanded source, lowered body, module definition, executable's facts). Same whether the rescue sits in the macro body or in a def the macro calls, and at item or expression position.

Telemetry: the macro's root_backend_product drive is deferred twice; materialized_executable waits on ExecutableFacts, ReturnType and RuntimeDemand for the macro function and no job completes them.

Untested today: fixtures 00889, 01148, 01199, 01312 have defmacro and try, but the try is always in an ordinary function. Lead, unverified: .agent/docs/exceptions.md (~409) says macro expansion runs without the entry that wraps ordinary code; if try/rescue lowering or its executable facts assume that entry, a macro root may never get those facts.

Blocks fz-sc8.144: Elixir's defstruct escapes each default inside try/rescue ArgumentError and re-raises "invalid default value for struct field ..., cannot escape ...".

Done when: the probe prints 7 on interp, run and build, pinned by a fixture; the cause is fixed where macro roots and try/rescue meet, not special-cased.
title: A macro whose compiled program uses try/rescue compiles, as in Elixir
